cards.english: Direct object pronouns — the full set (me / te / lo·la / nos / los·las)
cards.grammarNote:
A **direct object** receives the action of the verb. Replace it with a **direct object pronoun** that matches the person (and gender/number for third person). The pronoun goes **before** the conjugated verb.

**¿El café? Lo quiero.** → *lo* replaces *el café*.

table.title: Direct object pronouns
table.note: lo/la and los/las must match the gender and number of the noun they replace.

cards.english: lo/la replaces a noun to avoid repetition (it — the bread / the salad)
cards.grammarNote:
To avoid repeating a noun, replace it with **lo** (masculine) or **la** (feminine). The pronoun goes **before** the conjugated verb.

*Compro el pan.* → **Lo** compro. | *Compro la ensalada.* → **La** compro.
cards.englishPhrase: I buy the bread. → I buy it.

cards.english: lo/la/los/las must match the gender AND number of the noun replaced
cards.grammarNote:
**lo** = masc. singular (el pan, el queso…)
**la** = fem. singular (la ensalada, la leche…)
**los** = masc. plural (los huevos, los platos…)
**las** = fem. plural (las galletas, las manzanas…)

Always match the replaced noun, not the English 'it/them'.
cards.englishPhrase: The bread — I want it. The salad — I want it. The cookies — I want them.
cards.phrase: El pan — lo quiero. La ensalada — la quiero. Las galletas — las quiero.

produce.task: Give the correct pronoun for: the bread (masc. sg.), the salad (fem. sg.), the cookies (fem. pl.)
produce.gloss: lo → masc. sg. | la → fem. sg. | las → fem. pl.

cards.english: Pronoun placement: before a conjugated verb OR attached to an infinitive (both correct)
cards.grammarNote:
With **conjugated verb + infinitive**, the direct object pronoun has two equally correct positions:
1. **Before the conjugated verb**: *Lo quiero comprar.*
2. **Attached to the infinitive**: *Quiero comprarlo.*

Both mean the same thing.

contrast.prompt: Both are correct — where does 'lo' go?

cards.english: With estar + gerund, pronoun attaches to the gerund (with accent) OR goes before estar
cards.grammarNote:
With **estar + gerund**, the direct object pronoun has two positions:
1. **Before estar**: *Lo estoy mirando.*
2. **Attached to the gerund** (written accent required): *Estoy **mirándolo**.*

When you attach the pronoun, add an accent to keep the original stress on the gerund.

cloze.prompt: I am watching it — attach the pronoun to the gerund

cards.grammarNote: The **indirect object pronoun** marks the recipient — 'to/for whom'. It goes **before** the conjugated verb. **me** = to me, **te** = to you, **le** = to him/her/usted, **nos** = to us, **les** = to them.
cards.englishPhrase: I give the menu to him (the waiter).
cards.phrase: Le doy el menú al camarero.

table.title: Indirect Object Pronouns
table.note: Pronoun goes before the conjugated verb.

cards.english: le = to him/her with dar and decir
cards.grammarNote: Use **le** when the recipient is 'him', 'her', or 'usted'. It always goes **before** the verb: **le** doy, **le** digo, **le** escribo.
cards.englishPhrase: I give the cake to María.
cards.phrase: Le doy el pastel a María.

cloze.prompt: to her (María) — I give the cake

cards.word: Le doy el café a María.
cards.grammarNote: In Spanish, **le** and **a + person** are used **together**. The pronoun (le/les) is required even when you also name the person with 'a'. This is normal, not redundant.
cards.englishPhrase: I give the coffee to María.
cards.phrase: Le doy el café a María.

produce.task: Say 'I give the coffee to María' — use both le and a María.
produce.answer: Le doy el café a María.
produce.gloss: le + a María together is normal in Spanish — the pronoun is never dropped

cards.english: gustar in reverse: IO pronoun marks who likes it
cards.word: me gusta / te gusta / le gusta
cards.grammarNote: With **gustar**, the thing liked is the **subject** (gusta = singular, gustan = plural). The IO pronoun marks **who** likes it. So: 'I like coffee' = **me gusta** el café (literally: coffee pleases me).
cards.phrase: A ella le gusta el café.

table.title: gustar — reverse verb
table.note: gusta = one thing liked; gustan = multiple things liked.

cards.english: doler (to hurt) follows the same pattern as gustar
cards.grammarNote: **doler** works like gustar — the IO pronoun marks who feels the pain, and the verb agrees with the body part. **me duele** (one part) vs. **me duelen** (plural: los pies, las manos).
cards.phrase: Me duele la cabeza. (Me duelen los pies.)

cards.english: lo (direct) vs. le (indirect): sees him vs. gives to him
cards.word: lo veo / le doy el café
cards.grammarNote: **lo** = direct object — the person/thing directly receiving the action (who/what is seen, bought, etc.). **le** = indirect object — the recipient of something ('to/for whom'). When you give, say, or write *something* **to** someone, that 'someone' gets **le**.
cards.englishPhrase: I see him; I give him the coffee.
cards.phrase: Lo veo; le doy el café.

contrast.prompt: Which pronoun: sees him (direct) or gives to him (indirect)?

b.gloss: I give him the coffee → indirect object / recipient (le)

cards.english: Double object pronouns: indirect always comes first
cards.word: me lo / te la / nos los
cards.grammarNote: When a sentence has TWO object pronouns, the **indirect pronoun comes first**, then the direct: **indirect + direct**.
cards.englishPhrase: The coffee? The waiter gives it to me.
cards.phrase: ¿El café? Me lo da el camarero.

table.title: Two pronouns: indirect + direct
table.note: Order is always: indirect first, then direct.

cards.english: le/les + lo/la → se lo / se la (never le lo)
cards.grammarNote: When **le** or **les** appears before **lo / la / los / las**, the **le/les becomes se**. **Le lo** is never allowed → always **se lo**.
cards.englishPhrase: The menu? I give it to María.
cards.phrase: ¿El menú? Se lo doy a María.

cloze.text: El menú, a María → ___ lo doy.

cards.word: se lo doy / se lo dice
cards.grammarNote: **le** or **les** + **lo/la** → **se lo / se la**. The indirect object can be clarified with 'a + name': **se lo doy a María**.
cards.englishPhrase: I give it (the coffee) to María. He tells it to her.
cards.phrase: Se lo doy a María. Él se lo dice.

produce.task: Give it (the coffee) to María; tell it to her.
produce.answer: Se lo doy a María. Él se lo dice.
produce.gloss: le + lo is never allowed → se lo; indirect always first

cards.english: Double pronouns: before conjugated verb OR attached to infinitive
cards.word: te lo quiero dar / quiero dártelo
cards.grammarNote: With an infinitive, both pronouns can go **before the conjugated verb** (separate) or **attached together to the infinitive** (add written accent).
cards.englishPhrase: I want to give it to you.
cards.phrase: Te lo quiero dar. / Quiero dártelo.

contrast.prompt: Where do the double pronouns go with an infinitive?

cards.english: Full production: order + se lo rule together
cards.word: te lo compro / se la doy
cards.grammarNote: Combine both rules: **indirect first + direct second**, and **le → se** before lo/la. El pastel (masc.) → **lo**; la cuenta (fem.) → **la**.
cards.englishPhrase: I buy it (the cake) for you. I give it (the bill) to the waiter.
cards.phrase: Te lo compro. Se la doy al camarero.

produce.task: I buy it (the cake) for you; I give it (the bill) to the waiter.
produce.answer: Te lo compro. Se la doy al camarero.
produce.gloss: el pastel → lo (masc.); la cuenta → la (fem.); le + la → se la
